answer_text:
We want to evaluate

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2\binom{2n}{n}}.
\]

Use the beta integral

\[
B(n,n+1)=\int_0^1 x^{n-1}(1-x)^n\,dx
=\frac{(n-1)!\,n!}{(2n)!}.
\]

But

\[
\frac{1}{n\binom{2n}{n}}
=\frac{n!n!}{n(2n)!}
=\frac{(n-1)!\,n!}{(2n)!}.
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{1}{n\binom{2n}{n}}
=\int_0^1 x^{n-1}(1-x)^n\,dx.
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{n^2\binom{2n}{n}}
=\frac1n\int_0^1 x^{n-1}(1-x)^n\,dx.
\]

Summing over \(n\ge 1\),

\[
S=\int_0^1 \frac1x \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(x(1-x))^n}{n}\,dx.
\]

Since \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{n}=-\ln(1-z)\), we get

\[
S=\int_0^1 -\frac{\ln(1-x(1-x))}{x}\,dx
=\int_0^1 -\frac{\ln(x^2-x+1)}{x}\,dx.
\]

Now factor

\[
x^2-x+1=\frac{1+x^3}{1+x}.
\]

Thus

\[
-\ln(x^2-x+1)=\ln(1+x)-\ln(1+x^3),
\]

so

\[
S=\int_0^1 \frac{\ln(1+x)}{x}\,dx
-\int_0^1 \frac{\ln(1+x^3)}{x}\,dx.
\]

For the first integral,

\[
\int_0^1 \frac{\ln(1+x)}{x}\,dx
=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n^2}
=\frac{\pi^2}{12}.
\]

For the second integral, substitute \(u=x^3\), so \(dx/x=\frac13 du/u\):

\[
\int_0^1 \frac{\ln(1+x^3)}{x}\,dx
=\frac13\int_0^1 \frac{\ln(1+u)}{u}\,du
=\frac13\cdot\frac{\pi^2}{12}
=\frac{\pi^2}{36}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S=\frac{\pi^2}{12}-\frac{\pi^2}{36}
=\frac{\pi^2}{18}.
\]

Since

\[
\zeta(2)=\frac{\pi^2}{6},
\]

we have

\[
S=\frac13\zeta(2).
\]

Thus

\[
A=1,\qquad B=3,\qquad C=2.
\]

So

\[
A+B+C=1+3+2=6.
\]

\[
\boxed{6}
\]
